study.title: Chilika Lake, Odisha
study.question: How much of the apparent dry-season water-extent signal is seasonal or turbidity-driven versus a longer-term change between matched years?
limitations: Water level and seasonality dominate; no hydrological cause claims.
Brackish turbidity shifts NDWI/MNDWI values.

aoi.kind: hand-chosen rectangular working window near Satapada
aoi.boundary_source: Manually placed over lagoon/barrier area; not an official boundary.

can_conclude: Candidate surface-water extent signals (NDWI/MNDWI threshold classes) for matched dry-season and matched post-monsoon pairs.
That dry-season and post-monsoon signals must be read together: the pair-level difference between seasons bounds how much of any 2020-to-2025 change could be seasonal.
Per-pixel observation support (how many valid acquisitions back each composite pixel).
cannot_conclude: Permanent wetland loss or gain: water level, seasonality and turbidity dominate this site.
Hydrological causes, discharge changes or any claim about the lagoon mouth.
interpretation.note: The dry-season pair at this window is broadly similar between 2020 and 2025; seasonal amplitude at this particular window is modest because it sits over the main lagoon. Seasonal sensitivity is documented by comparing the two experiments, not by a single pair.

attribution: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2020-2026), processed by ESA; L2A products distributed by the Element 84 Earth Search STAC catalogue (AWS Open Data). DEM: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA/DLR) where included. Event context: NDRRMA (2025) and ICIMOD (2026) situation reporting, cited as external literature, not project measurements.

catalog.license: Copernicus Sentinel data: free, open and unrestricted use with attribution (ESA Copernicus data policy). Catalogue: Element 84 Earth Search, AWS Open Data.

area_cross_check.method: projected polygon area, independent geodesic area on the WGS84 ellipsoid, and rasterised pixel-count area on the analysis grid
area_cross_check.note: the raster area differs from the polygon area by boundary rasterisation only; hectares and km2 are converted from projected square metres, not from degrees

limitations: Water level and seasonality dominate; no hydrological cause claims.
Brackish turbidity shifts NDWI/MNDWI values.
The following indices use 20 m SWIR bands resampled to the 10 m analysis grid and contain no genuine 10 m SWIR detail: mndwi.
Composites are robust within-period summaries of a few observations, not a dense time series; inter-annual change is represented by two period composites only.
Index differences are candidate spectral signals. They are not verified deforestation, wetland loss, construction, glacier damage or any other causal land-cover label.
Cloud, shadow and saturated-pixel exclusion relies on the provider SCL product; terrain shadow is not independently re-derived.
Surface reflectance is the provider L2A product; no independent atmospheric correction is performed.
Areas are planimetric on the documented projected grid; UTM scale distortion at this AOI is small but nonzero.
